A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SMI study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Added figures and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-distribution experiments, Gaussian-channel results in Table 1, and MNIST representation-learning outcomes in Figure 5, with additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on structured synthetic images in Appendix C and Figure 10.

M1.justification: The SMI variants, KSG estimation and random slicing, and MI-versus-SMI representation-learning procedures are unchanged. The added image experiments apply the existing measures without introducing an algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds Gaussian-blob and rectangle image distributions with known mutual information, extending dependence benchmarking to structured synthetic images. The original four vector-distribution families, Gaussian-channel task, and MNIST coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the MI, SMI, and 2-SMI comparisons under whitening and standardization; Figure 5 retains MI-versus-SMI training. Figure 10 varies projection rank within the existing k-SMI family without adding a baseline method.

E3.justification: The added image experiment evaluates 16×16 and 32×32 inputs with projection ranks k = 1, 2, 3, 5, and 7. Figure 10 specifies 10,000 estimation samples and 128 projection samples. Settings of the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 10 extends projection-rank sensitivity analysis to structured images, showing whether increasing k avoids saturation at two image resolutions. Existing dimensionality, randomized-parameter, and representation-collapse analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report synthetic results using means and standard deviations across ten runs. Figure 10 follows this existing practice; retained experiments have no changed run counts or uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds saturation curves for four image-family/resolution combinations, with higher plateaus at larger projection ranks. Existing numerical results and plotted curves are unchanged, including Table 1 and the appendix plots renumbered from Figures 6–8 to Figures 7–9.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.1 tightens the Gaussian SMI saturation bound from 3/(d−1) to 1/(d−1). Appendix B revises the digamma-bound argument and corrects the Euler-integral normalization from Γ((d−2)/2) to Γ((d−1)/2). The exact SMI expression and remaining theorem statements are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and discussion retain the same central claims about saturation, redundancy bias, dimensional decay, and slicing tradeoffs. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The substantive explanations of redundancy bias, saturation, and dimensional decay remain unchanged. Appendix C presents the added results as confirmation. Section 7 retains its original limitations, including the now-outdated statement that structured-image synthetic tests are absent.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds brief generation information: the image datasets use MI-preserving smooth injective mappings from [34] to reproduce datasets from [17]. Figure 10 supplies sampling settings. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, runtime, and implementation-source disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning relative to earlier SMI research are unchanged. The added experiment reuses already-cited works [17] and [34] for dataset provenance and construction.

P1.justification: Changes include updated affiliations and contact details, a short addition to Appendix C, and local proof wording and equation-numbering edits. The title, abstract, main narrative, and section order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds image examples in Figure 6 and a four-panel results display in Figure 10. Existing appendix figures are renumbered, Table 2 moves from page 17 to page 18, and nearby text reflows. Existing plots and the overall visual design are preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision through the normalization correction and tighter bound, and adds structured-image evidence beyond v1's synthetic vector tests. These are useful, limited gains while the primary results and conclusions remain stable. The unchanged Section 7 statement excluding structured-image tests creates an inconsistency, but does not outweigh the added evidence and mathematical refinements.
